brief:
# Artemis approved-facts pilot — AI first-pass review

You give a first opinion on fact candidates that rules extracted from the 2026-10-19 Korean visa/stay manuals. A person makes the actual decision later; your output is shown to them as "AI 1차 의견", never as an approval. This is not a legal verification: a fact only says "this manual page says this".

## Input (read-only)
`packets/chunkN.json` in this directory:
- `roles`: the allowed role ids and their Korean names.
- `pages`: page id → {title, text, domain}. `domain` is `visa_issuance` (사증 매뉴얼) or `stay` (체류 매뉴얼).
- `candidates`: each has `candidate_id`, `subject` (status_code, sub_code, procedure, qualifiers), `role` (may be null), `role_from_check`, `value` (kind money|period, amount, unit krw|usd|free|day|month|year, comparator), `source` (page_id, quote = an exact substring of the page text).
The rules guessed subject and role from nearby words and the nearest status code ABOVE the value in the page text; those guesses are often wrong. OCR has flattened tables, so a row like "소득기준 23,595,948 30,152,118 …" lost its column headers — read the surrounding page text to work out what each number belongs to.

Do not read or change anything else. Write only your output file.

## For every candidate decide
- `ai_decision`:
  - `approve` — the quote states a real rule-level fact (a fee, an income threshold, a deposit, a deadline, a validity, a stay period or cap, an extension period, a waiting period, a count limit) and you can tell from the page **whom it applies to and what it is**.
  - `reject` — not a fact: an example ("※ 예시"), a reference point inside another sentence that is not itself a rule, a date/year, a page number, a statute article number, OCR garbage, a duplicate of another candidate in the same packet, or a number that belongs to a sentence about something else.
  - `hold` — a real fact, but the page does not settle its subject, condition, or role (e.g. a flattened table whose column order you cannot recover with confidence). Say what a person must check.
- For `approve` and `hold`, give your best `subject`, `role` and `value`:
  - `subject.status_code` (e.g. "D-2"), `subject.sub_code` (e.g. "D-2-8") or null, `subject.procedure`: "visa" for a visa_issuance page, "stay" for a stay page (never mix).
  - `subject.qualifiers`: `applicant` (본인 / 동반가족 / 초청인 / 사업주 or null), `household_size` (number or null), `per` (e.g. "1명당", "연간" or null), `nationality` (or null), `row_label`, `column_label` (for table values, or null).
  - `role`: one id from `roles`. Use "other" only with a note.
  - `value`: keep `kind`, correct `amount`/`unit` if the rules misread them (the amount must appear in the quote), and set `comparator` to one of 이상, 이하, 이내, 미만, 초과, 까지, 동안, 간 or null.
- `reason`: Korean, 1–2 sentences: what the value is, whom it applies to, and why you decided so. For `hold`, what a person must check.
- `confidence`: high | medium | low.

Rules:
- Ground everything in the page text of the packet. Do not use outside knowledge to fill a subject or value the page does not state.
- Never change `source`. If the value is not in the quote, reject.
- When the status code above the value is wrong (the value is in a general section, or under another status), correct it or set it to null and hold.

## Output
Write `out/chunkN.json`: a JSON array, one object per candidate in packet order:
```json
{"candidate_id": "fc-…", "ai_decision": "approve|reject|hold", "subject": {…} or null, "role": "fee" or null, "value": {…} or null, "reason": "…", "confidence": "high|medium|low"}
```
Before writing, self-check with `python3 -I`: one object per candidate, same order, decisions in the allowed set, roles in `roles`, for approve/hold the amount appears in the quote (compare digits after removing commas; Korean units like 만/천 count). Report in four lines: counts of approve / reject / hold, the self-check result, and two example candidate ids with your reason.
